biography.plain_text: Kenneth Rainin was an American entrepreneur who founded Rainin Instrument Company in 1963 after graduating from Ohio State University and serving in the Army. He developed the laboratory-supplies business into a manufacturer known for pipettes, instruments used to measure and transfer small quantities of liquid, before selling it to Mettler-Toledo in 2001.

long_biography.plain_text:
Laboratory-instrument entrepreneur Kenneth Rainin helped finance the San Francisco Ballet's 2004 European tour and chaired its executive committee. His involvement in Bay Area institutions also included trusteeships at St. Mary's College in Moraga and Oakland's Head-Royce School. In medical research, he funded the creation of a centre at the University of California, San Francisco, devoted to colitis and Crohn's disease.

Before his death in 2007, Rainin worked with his daughter Jen to define the arts, education and health programmes of his foundation. He made the foundation the beneficiary of most of his estate, providing resources for those causes beyond his lifetime.
